metadata.headline: Why does Bolt work with fleet owners as well as individual drivers?

platform_lesson.title: Fleet owners help Bolt add several cars and drivers to a city at once
platform_lesson.text: Bolt's ride-hailing platform still depends on a simple local match: a rider needs a car, and a driver nearby has to be ready to provide the ride. What makes Bolt interesting is the extra fleet-owner layer that can help build this supply. Bolt says fleet partners use its platform in more than 45 countries. A fleet owner can add and manage several vehicles and drivers through the Fleet Portal instead of Bolt having to recruit every car one by one. In some markets this relationship is especially important; for example, Bolt's current German onboarding requires drivers to be registered in the Fleet Portal by a fleet owner. Drivers still provide the actual ride, so fleet owners are not the provider side of the marketplace. They are a partner that can bring more local transport capacity into the network. This helps explain how Bolt can run ride-hailing across 50 countries and more than 850 cities without owning most of the cars itself.

core_value_unit.explanation: A completed ride is the core value unit: a rider requests transport, Bolt matches the request with available local supply, and a driver takes the rider from pickup to destination.

actor.explanation: Bolt owns and operates the platform, connects riders with drivers, coordinates matching and payments, and sets participation rules.

metrics.note: Bolt says its broader mobility platform is available in more than 850 cities worldwide.

job.explanation: Bolt has to create enough rider demand and driver supply in each city so that trips can be matched quickly and drivers can find enough work.

gain.explanation: Bolt benefits when more rides are completed and when riders, drivers and fleet partners keep using the platform.

pain.explanation: Bolt can struggle when too few drivers are available in a local market and must also comply with different transport, licensing and labor rules.

transaction.explanation: Bolt coordinates ride requests, matching and payments and earns service fees from activity on the platform. Fee structures vary by market and service.

governance.explanation: Bolt sets platform requirements for drivers, vehicles, conduct, payments and safety while adapting them to local law.

promotion_channel.explanation: Riders enter mainly through the Bolt app, supported by local promotions and the wider Bolt brand across mobility services.

activities.explanation: Bolt runs the apps, matches ride requests with available supply, supports users, processes payments and manages marketplace quality.

resources.explanation: Important resources include the rider base, local supply, trip and location data, matching technology, payments infrastructure and the Bolt brand.

actor.explanation: People use Bolt when they want an on-demand ride from one place to another.

metrics.note: Bolt reports more than 200 million customers across its full mobility and delivery platform, not ride-hailing alone.

job.explanation: Riders want to arrange transport without having to find or negotiate with a driver themselves.

gain.explanation: The app makes it possible to request a ride, see trip information and pay through one digital service.

pain.explanation: Riders can face longer waits when few drivers are nearby, changing prices, cancellations or safety concerns.

transaction.explanation: The rider enters pickup and destination details, requests a ride and pays through a supported method.

filter.explanation: A ride can only be offered where Bolt operates and where suitable local supply is available.

access_channel.explanation: Riders mainly use the Bolt app to request and manage rides.

activities.explanation: Riders request transport, meet the driver, take the trip, pay and can rate the experience.

resources.explanation: Riders bring trip demand, pickup and destination data, payment information and ratings that help the marketplace operate.

actor.explanation: Drivers provide the actual transport service using an eligible vehicle and their time.

metrics.note: Bolt reports more than 4.5 million driver, courier and merchant partners across the whole platform. This is broader than ride-hailing drivers alone.

job.explanation: Drivers want access to nearby ride demand so they can turn available driving time into earnings.

gain.explanation: Bolt can bring drivers a stream of ride requests without each driver having to find passengers independently.

pain.explanation: Drivers may wait between rides and have to cover costs such as fuel or charging, insurance, maintenance, rental or financing.

transaction.explanation: Drivers receive trip opportunities, choose whether to accept them and complete the physical ride.

filter.explanation: Drivers and vehicles must meet the rules that apply in their local market before they can provide rides.

access_channel.explanation: Drivers use the Bolt Driver app to go online, receive ride requests and manage work on the platform.

activities.explanation: Drivers make themselves available, accept suitable rides, collect passengers, complete trips and keep required documents and vehicles in order.

resources.explanation: Drivers contribute their time, driving ability, local knowledge and access to an eligible vehicle and required documents.

actor.explanation: Fleet owners can bring several vehicles and drivers into Bolt and manage them through the Fleet Portal.

metrics.note: Bolt says fleet partners use its platform across more than 45 countries.

job.explanation: Fleet owners make vehicles and driver capacity available and keep that capacity organized for use on the platform.

gain.explanation: Fleet owners can connect their vehicles and drivers with a large source of passenger demand and manage performance through one portal.

pain.explanation: Fleet owners need enough trips to keep vehicles productive while handling licensing, documentation, maintenance and local regulation.

transaction.explanation: Fleet owners register vehicles and drivers and make that local transport capacity available to the Bolt network.

filter.explanation: Fleet companies, vehicles and drivers must meet local legal and Bolt requirements before they can be activated.

access_channel.explanation: Bolt provides fleet owners with a portal to add drivers and vehicles, track activity, view earnings and manage reports.

activities.explanation: Fleet owners register vehicles, add or recruit drivers, monitor activity and manage fleet administration.

resources.explanation: Fleet owners contribute groups of vehicles, access to drivers, operating licenses and local fleet-management capability.

metrics.note: Bolt says its broader mobility platform is available in more than 850 cities worldwide.
Bolt reports more than 200 million customers across its full mobility and delivery platform, not ride-hailing alone.
Bolt reports more than 4.5 million driver, courier and merchant partners across the whole platform.
Bolt says fleet partners use its platform across more than 45 countries.

current.explanation: The rider asks Bolt for a trip and pays through a supported method.
Bolt sends trip opportunities to eligible drivers based on location and local marketplace conditions.
Bolt shows the rider the matched driver, pickup information and estimated arrival details.
The driver provides the physical transport from pickup to destination.
Bolt coordinates payment and driver earnings after completed trips.
Fleet owners add groups of vehicles and drivers that can provide local ride supply on Bolt.

sources.title: About Bolt
sources.note: Primary source for Bolt's current scale: 200M+ customers, 4.5M+ driver/courier/merchant partners, 50+ countries, 850+ cities, and the statement that ride-hailing is Bolt's core service across 50 countries.

sources.title: Investor Relations
sources.note: Primary source for December 2025 platform-wide run-rate figures, including €12B+ GMV and €3B revenue, plus customer and partner scale.

sources.title: Join Bolt with your fleet
sources.note: Primary source for the fleet-owner role, the statement that Bolt is used by fleet partners across 45+ countries, and Fleet Portal functions for managing vehicles, drivers, earnings and recruitment.

sources.title: How to become a Bolt fleet owner and grow your business using the Fleet Portal
sources.note: Primary source explaining how fleet owners can add vehicles and drivers and manage a transport business through Bolt.

sources.title: Driver document requirements in Germany
sources.note: Current market example showing that in Germany a driver must first be registered in the Fleet Portal by a Fleet Owner before completing Bolt onboarding.

sources.title: Bolt Commission in Germany
sources.note: Example showing that Bolt service and commission fees vary by city and operator type, which is why the PBMC does not use the old generic 15–20% global commission claim.
